person.name: Norbert Moldován
person.title: Senior Bioinformatician
person.pitch: I build computational pipelines and predictive models for basic and translational research.

items.label: High-dimensional DNA and RNA-seq data
items.detail: What I build: I turn noisy NGS datasets into clean features models can learn from. How: QC, normalization, batch-aware feature engineering, coverage tracks, and long-read signal. Stack: Python, R, Bash. Case study: Genome-wide cfDNA characterization of patients with resectable esophageal cancer (https://pathsocjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/path.6175)

items.label: Deep learning and predictive models
items.detail: What I build: Classification, survival, and recurrence models from high-dimensional omics features. How: Nested cross-validation with calibrated probabilities, survival objectives, and Optuna-driven hyperparameter search. Stack: PyTorch, scikit-learn, Optuna, deployment-ready tooling. Case study: Multi-modal cfDNA patterns enhance cancer survival and recurrence analysis (https://www.cell.com/cell-reports-medicine/fulltext/S2666-3791(23)00566-9)

items.label: Embeddings, transformers, and diffusion models
items.detail: What I build: Representation learning and generative models for sequence and multi-modal genomic data. How: Pretrain or fine-tune sequence encoders and generative backbones, then probe embeddings for downstream phenotype tasks. Stack: PyTorch, Hugging Face, TensorFlow. Case study: cfDNA dataset augmentation using diffusion models (https://www.nwo.nl/en/projects/ngf160923005)

items.label: Production-ready bioinformatics tooling
items.detail: What I ship: Scripts and libraries labs can run, extend, and trust in day-to-day analysis. How: Agent-assisted development with typed interfaces, tests, and clear CLIs so analyses stay auditable under change. Languages: Python, R, Bash; agentic coding. Figures: Publication-ready plotting with ggplot2, ggsci, seaborn, and matplotlib. Case study: FrEIA — Fragment End Integrated Analysis pipeline (https://github.com/mouliere-lab/FrEIA)

items.label: Reproducible workflow orchestration
items.detail: What I build: Scalable pipeline DAGs with locked environments that reproduce across machines. How: Pin environments, declare rule graphs, and checkpoint intermediates so reruns are deterministic and reviewable. Orchestration: Snakemake, Mamba/Conda, Git. Case study: Comparison of cell-free and small extracellular vesicle derived DNA in plasma of lung cancer patients (https://www.cell.com/iscience/fulltext/S2589-0042(24)01967-9)

items.label: Slurm HPC and accelerated compute
items.detail: What I build: Cluster jobs that scale CPU and GPU work without reinventing the scheduler. How: Array jobs, resource-aware GPU allocation, and multi-threaded steps tuned to node topology and queue limits. Runtime: Slurm, multi-threading, GPU acceleration. Case study: Early outcome prediction in Large B-Cell Lymphoma (https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.05.29.26353426v1)

items.label: cfDNA genomics, epigenomics, and fragmentomics
items.detail: What I deliver: Multi-omic liquid biopsy signals for detection, monitoring, and MRD. How: Derive fragment-end, length, methylation, and CNV features from plasma WGS/WGBS and train models against clinical endpoints. Readouts: Fragmentomics, methylation, copy-number and mutation features from plasma cfDNA. Case study: The effect of preanalytical variables on cfDNA fragmentation (https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article-abstract/68/6/803/6549200)

items.label: Short- and long-read sequencing analysis
items.detail: What I build: Platform-aware workflows that combine short-read depth with long-read structure. How: Hybrid pipelines that pair Illumina depth for calling with ONT/PacBio span for isoforms, SVs, and haplotype context. Platforms: Illumina, Oxford Nanopore Technologies, PacBio. Case studies: Real-time analysis of cfDNA from plasma and urine (https://link.springer.com/article/10.15252/emmm.202217282) Multi-platform integration reveals novel transcriptome of a virus (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/microbiology/articles/10.3389/fmicb.2017.02708/full)

items.label: DNA, RNA from liquid biopsies and beyond
items.detail: What I build: End-to-end DNA and RNA processing pipelines. How: From demultiplexing through alignment, quantification, and differential analysis to ranked biomarker candidates. Focus: Translational methods that move from raw reads to biomarker candidates. Case studies: The effect of preanalytical variables on cfDNA fragmentation (https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article-abstract/68/6/803/6549200)

works.title: FrEIA
works.subtitle: Fragment End Integrated Analysis
works.problem: Shallow WGS is affordable but lacks the depth needed for conventional mutation-based ctDNA detection.
works.method: Snakemake pipeline extracting cfDNA fragment-end sequence proportions and diversity, integrating copy-number aberration, fragment size, and end-sequence features into a FrEIA score with machine-learning classification for cancer detection.
works.impact: Open-source toolkit used in multi-modal cfDNA genomic and fragmentomic analyses for cancer survival and recurrence.

works.title: ITSFASTR
works.subtitle: Ultra-fast cfDNA analysis · ONT · Illumina
works.problem: Long (>500 bp) cell-free DNA fragments from nanopore sequencing challenge assumptions about tumor-derived fragment length in liquid biopsy.
works.method: End-to-end bioinformatics pipeline for real-time analysis of the cancer genome and fragmentome from plasma and urine cfDNA using Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing data.
works.impact: Pipeline and study published in EMBO Molecular Medicine, demonstrating the value of long-reads for liquid biopsy.

works.title: Ouro-tools
works.subtitle: Circular RNA from long-read liquid biopsies
works.problem: Full-length circular RNA in liquid biopsies is hard to recover and quantify with short-read-centric workflows, limiting its use as a cancer biomarker.
works.method: Preprocessing and analysis pipeline for circular RNA from Oxford Nanopore sequencing of liquid biopsy material, developed under ZonMw funding for cervical cancer detection.
works.impact: ZonMw grant (2023): Full-length Circular RNA Detection in Liquid Biopsies for Cervical Cancer Detection. Companion tooling for ONT circRNA workflows.

featured.title: Multi-modal cell-free DNA genomic and fragmentomic patterns enhance cancer survival and recurrence analysis
featured.problem: Tumor-derived cfDNA is cleaved differently from healthy DNA, but shallow WGS needs robust end-sequence metrics to turn that biology into a detection signal.
featured.method: Snakemake pipeline extracting fragment-end sequence proportions and diversity, integrating copy-number aberration, fragment size, and end-sequence features into a FrEIA score with machine-learning classification for cancer detection.
featured.impact: Open-source toolkit used in multi-modal cfDNA genomic and fragmentomic analyses for cancer survival and recurrence.

featured.problem: Long (>500 bp) cell-free DNA fragments from nanopore sequencing challenge assumptions about tumor-derived fragment length in liquid biopsy.
featured.method: End-to-end bioinformatics pipeline for real-time analysis of the cancer genome and fragmentome from plasma and urine cfDNA using Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencing data.
featured.impact: Pipeline and study published in EMBO Molecular Medicine, demonstrating long-read fragmentomics for liquid biopsy.

featured.title: Third-generation Sequencing Reveals Extensive Polycistronism and Transcriptional Overlapping in a Baculovirus
featured.problem: Short-read assays under-resolve overlapping and polycistronic transcription in compact viral genomes, obscuring true transcript architecture.
featured.method: PacBio long-read sequencing of Autographa californica multiple nucleopolyhedrovirus RNA to map full-length isoforms, polycistronic RNAs, and transcriptional overlaps.
featured.impact: First-author Scientific Reports study establishing long-read isoform mapping for a prototype baculovirus transcriptome.
